relevance_note: A case report of a Blau syndrome patient with a NOD2 variant plus literature tables of individual BS patients: 'He was diagnosed with BS by the finding of a variant of the NOD2 gene (R334W)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper including the two converted supplementary tables. A short Python script (scratch dir) parsed the Supplementary Table 1 (24 BS patients with hypertension) and Supplementary Table 2 (38 BS patients with digestive system involvement) rows; the per-row feature items were listed by hand from the cells and the script asserted each item is a verbatim substring of its cell; all spans were then checked verbatim against the paper. Labels: the 'Patient/age/sex' column starts with a bare index number, so table patients are 'Table S1 #n' and 'Table S2 #n'. The second element of that column is recorded as age_at_last_evaluation (the text calls it 'age at baseline evaluation'; units are years unless printed as 'mo'). NOT MERGED although probably the same people (same reference, age, sex and variant): S1#2/S2#21, S1#4/S2#3, S1#6/S2#18, S1#14/S2#23, S1#15/S2#31, S1#16/S2#24, S1#17/S2#30, S1#20/S2#28, S1#21/S2#14, S1#23/S2#22, S1#24/S2#38; the paper does not state the overlap. Table cells '+' read as observed; the word 'none' in the Skin rash/Arthritis/Uveitis columns read as excluded (no symbol legend needed; it is a word). Empty cells are not reported. Abbreviations expanded from the table legends, quoted as an extra span. The 'Familial vs. Sporadic' column (F/S) has no schema field and was not used for inheritance. Every S1 patient gets an observed hypertension row from the table title; HT onset column used as onset. In S2, 'Age at onset of digestive system' is used as onset of the digestive-manifestation features. Zygosity 'heterozygous' for S2 #1-#14 (the 14 hepatic-granuloma patients; refs 5, 7, 11, 16, 20-27) carrying R334Q, C495Y, E383D or M513T comes from the Discussion sentence naming these variants in that group; E498G, P268S and M491L in that group were not given a zygosity by the paper. Contradiction/inconsistencies: the Discussion lists 'E268S' among the hepatic-granuloma variants while Table S2 #8 prints 'P268S' (recorded as printed in the table); the text says all 14 hepatic granulomas were proven by liver biopsy, but S2 #6, #7 and #11 have 'HG' without the biopsy asterisk. S2 #26 has three NOD2 entries ('P268S, IVS8+158, 1007 fs') recorded as three variant rows; '1007 fs' and 'IVS8+158' have no protein/cDNA field filled. Table variants without 'p.' prefix are recorded as protein_hgvs_as_stated. Case patient: the paper calls the variant 'de novo' but reports no parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Age 19 at presentation is used as age at last evaluation (no age at last follow-up given); no age at diagnosis stated. Uveitis and cataract excluded from 'without ocular lesions'; glaucoma and visual impairment left not reported; note he had unexplained eye redness before age 10. Inflammatory markers were elevated in childhood (ESR 27, CRP 36.5) and normal at last follow-up: both rows emitted, checklist 'observed' because the person had them (time-separated, not a same-time contradiction). Ceruloplasmin 'negative' left unrecorded (unclear which abnormality it rules out). Vasculitis for the case patient from the Discussion ('large-vessel vasculitis resembling Takayasu arteritis, just like our patient'). Discussion-level groups (e.g. '24 patients with hypertension') were not used for exclusion. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null (no single stated total of NOD2-variant patients); cites_prior_report is null because literature-review patients are attributed per row in source_reference_in_review.
